lines: Concerns about his mood and behavior over the past month, brought by his daughter due to increasing withdrawal and loss of interest in hobbies.
A 67-year-old man is brought to the primary care clinic by his daughter due to concerns about his mood and behavior over the past month.
She says that he has become increasingly withdrawn and has lost interest in his usual hobbies, such as gardening and watching football.
He spends most of the day lying in bed and requires prompting to eat or shower.
He complains of waking up around 3 AM and being unable to fall back asleep.
He denies suicidal thoughts but admits to feeling “tired of everything.” He has unintentionally lost 5 kg (11 lb) over the past 3 weeks.

encounters.cc: Progressive swelling in his lower extremities over the past 3 weeks since starting nifedipine.

lines: Progressive swelling in his lower extremities over the past 3 weeks since starting nifedipine.

The patient is a 70-year-old male with coronary artery disease, prior myocardial infarctions, and recent cardiac catheterization complicated by contrast reaction who returns for evaluation of progressive lower extremity edema.
He states that his ankles and feet feel heavy by the evening and that his shoes no longer fit properly by dinnertime.
Each morning, the swelling is mostly resolved but worsens again throughout the day.
He denies any shortness of breath, orthopnea, or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea.
There is no chest pain, palpitations, or recent weight gain.
He denies recent travel, changes in diet, or prolonged immobility.
- Mobitz type I atrioventricular block (Wenckebach phenomenon) (diagnosed 2021-01-15)
- History of myocardial infarction (3 years prior)
- History of myocardial infarction (6 months prior)
- Major depressive disorder, in partial remission
His past medical history includes hypertension, stable angina, and osteoarthritis.
- Cardiac catheterization with drug-eluting stent placement (3 years ago)
He takes multiple medications including lisinopril, metoprolol, low-dose aspirin, simvastatin, acetaminophen as needed for joint pain, and nifedipine for blood pressure that was started 2 months ago.
He has been on the same medication regimen for several months without any recent changes.
He reports adherence to all prescribed medications.
- Nifedipine extended-release 30 mg daily (started 2 months ago)
Iodinated contrast media - anaphylactoid reaction (flushing, hypotension, obtundation)
He is retired and enjoys walking his dog each morning and gardening in the afternoon.
He sleeps well and has not noticed any cough, wheezing, or night sweats.
He drinks alcohol socially and has never smoked.
On review of systems, he denies muscle pain, urinary symptoms, or skin changes.
His appetite is normal and he has not experienced fatigue or dizziness.
On physical exam, vital signs are within normal limits.
His blood pressure today is 132/78 mm Hg.
Cardiopulmonary examination is unremarkable, with no rales, wheezing, or murmurs.
His jugular veins are not distended.
There is 2+ bilateral pitting edema of the ankles that extends to the mid-shin.
No erythema or warmth is noted.
Abdominal exam is benign with no hepatosplenomegaly or ascites.
There are no bruits, and bowel sounds are normal.
Neurologic exam shows normal reflexes and strength.
Laboratory studies including creatinine, liver function tests, and urinalysis are within normal limits.
Chest x-ray is clear, with no signs of pulmonary congestion or cardiomegaly.
An ECG shows normal sinus rhythm.
